seoSectionTitle: Password-protect PDF online — free and secure
seoP1: Our Protect PDF tool lets you add a password to any PDF document so only people who know the password can open it. The file is encrypted with strong 256-bit AES encryption, a standard also used in banking and government. The file stays protected wherever it travels.
seoP2: Upload your PDF, choose a password, and download the protected file. The encryption is applied to the file itself, so the password is required every time the document is opened — on any device, in any PDF reader, by email or in the cloud.
seoP3: Uploaded files are transferred over a secure encrypted connection, scanned for malware, and automatically deleted from our servers within 1 hour. We never store your password. Encrypting a PDF is completely lossless, so your text and images keep their original quality. There is no watermark.

diveTitle: What actually happens when you protect a PDF
diveSubtitle: What the encryption covers and what it doesn't.
dive1Desc: This tool applies 256-bit AES encryption, a standard also used in banking and government, to require a password before the PDF can be opened. This is meaningfully stronger than the weaker 40-bit or 128-bit encryption some older PDF tools still default to.
dive2Title: Setting permissions vs. setting a password
dive2Desc: You can require a password just to open the file, restrict actions like printing, copying text, or editing even after opening, or both at once. These are independent settings — you could, for example, let anyone open the file but block printing.
dive3Title: Can the protection be removed later?
dive3Desc: Yes, with our Unlock PDF tool — but only if you know the password you set. There's no backdoor or master key; if the password is lost, the file's content is genuinely inaccessible, which is the entire point of real encryption.
dive4Title: Does protecting change the file content?
dive4Desc: No — protection only adds an encryption and permissions layer around the existing content. Text, images, and formatting are completely unchanged; the file just requires a password and enforces the permission rules you set.
dive5Desc: If a PDF already has a password, you'll need to unlock it first before applying new protection settings — you can't stack a second password on top of an existing one. Unlock, then re-protect with your new settings.
dive6Desc: The encryption is only as strong as the password protecting it — a short or common password is the weak point, not the encryption algorithm. Aim for at least 12 characters mixing letters, numbers, and symbols, and avoid reusing a password you use elsewhere.
faq1A: Yes. You can password-protect PDF files online for free, with no watermark.
faq2A: We use 256-bit AES encryption — a widely used industry-standard algorithm.
faq3A: No. Your password is used only to encrypt the file during processing and is never stored. Uploaded files are auto-deleted within 1 hour.
faq4Q: What happens if I forget the password?
faq4A: We cannot recover it — that is the point of strong encryption. Please store your password somewhere safe before sharing the file.
faq5Q: Can I remove the password later?
faq5A: Yes. Use our Unlock PDF tool with the correct password to remove the protection whenever you need to.
